original_question: For each prime p and field F, must the p-primary component of the Brauer group satisfy one of the following: it is zero, it contains a nonzero divisible subgroup, or else p = 2 and the 2-primary component is an elementary abelian 2-group?
target_in_paper: Section 11.D, Conjecture 11.6 (the Brumer-Rosen Conjecture), introduced immediately after Problem 11.5 as the finer conjecture refining the question of which finite cardinalities of Br(F) can occur. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost exactly: it is about a field F, a prime p, the p-primary component of Br(F), and the same three alternatives listed in Conjecture 11.6, including the exceptional p = 2 elementary abelian case. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states this as a named conjecture, Conjecture 11.6 (Brumer-Rosen), not as a theorem or a general informal question. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, the ambient group should be identified explicitly as the classical Brauer group Br(F) of a field F, using the notation (Br(F))_p for its p-primary component. The Brauer group notation is set up in Section 0, and the decomposition into p-primary components is stated immediately before Conjecture 11.6. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

The paper's quantifier order is 'for a given field F and each prime p'; your draft reverses the order, which is mathematically equivalent but slightly less faithful to the official formulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
Alternative (b) should be read as a subgroup of (Br(F))_p itself: the p-primary component contains a nonzero divisible subgroup. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

Alternative (c) should identify the 2-primary component precisely as an elementary abelian 2-group, i.e. a vector space over F_2; this is the only exceptional case allowed. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

The nearby context says this conjecture is the finer statement meant to sharpen Problem 11.5 about which finite sizes of Brauer groups can occur; that motivation is omitted from the draft, though it is not part of the formal conjecture. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
refined_question: Let F be a field, let Br(F) denote its classical Brauer group, and for a prime p let (Br(F))_p be the p-primary component of Br(F), i.e. the subgroup consisting of Brauer classes of p-power order. Is the Brumer-Rosen Conjecture true: for every field F and every prime p, must one of the following hold: (a) (Br(F))_p = 0; (b) (Br(F))_p contains a nonzero divisible subgroup; or (c) p = 2 and (Br(F))_2 is an elementary abelian 2-group? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 11.D rather than the paper's early crossed-product problems: the distinctive trichotomy 'zero / contains a nonzero divisible subgroup / p = 2 and elementary abelian 2-group' appears verbatim only in Conjecture 11.6. Because your draft already reproduces that trichotomy accurately, it is highly complete; the main repairs are to name the conjecture, make Br(F) and (Br(F))_p explicit, and add the immediate setup that Br(F) is being decomposed into p-primary components in order to refine Problem 11.5. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
